newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA, NEW ZEALAND FINISH BILATERAL TRADE TALKS.
newsitem.headline: CHINA, NEW ZEALAND FINISH BILATERAL TRADE TALKS.

text.p: China and New Zealand have reached agreement on bilateral market access in areas related to Beijing's long-delayed bid to enter the World Trade Organisation (WTO), the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
The agreement, which appeared to focus on market access for major New Zealand exports to China such as wool, was signed by Long Yongtu, China's top negotiator for entrance to the WTO, Xinhua said.
New Zealand's deputy minister of foreign relations and trade, Alastair Bisley, signed the deal for Wellington, and Beijing's foreign trade minister, Wu Yi, attended the ceremony, the agency said.
Xinhua gave no details on the content of the agreement, but Wellington has pushed Beijing to lower tariffs on wool, one of New Zealand's biggest exports to China.
Trade between the two countries is worth more than $900 million a year, with the balance in China's favour.
The talks marked the first time a country had discussed market access with China under the framework of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), the forerunner to the WTO, Xinhua said.
The deal would help boost trade between the two countries and would aid Beijing's efforts to win membership in the WTO, it said.
"The fact that this time New Zealand took the lead to reach an agreement with China on this matter will add a strong impetus to the process of multilateral talks on China's access to WTO," it said.
Beijing's entrance to the body has been stalled over iss as access to its potentially huge markets, transparency in government procurement, tariff barriers and subsidies for China's state companies.

Beijing has argued it should be allowed to join the WTO under the more lenient terms granted developing countries but many nations, in particular the United States, say China's economy is too big for such treatment.
The White House said on Monday there had been little progress in China's bid to join the global trade club, but did not rule out the possibility an accord might be reached by the end of the year.
U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky on Wednesday said Washington would not rush to conclude an agreement with Beijing on the terms of its entry.
